questions.a: C) Tiredness. Tiredness increases reaction time; the others affect braking distance.

questions.q: Is force a scalar or a vector?
Hooke's law: extension is proportional to...
Big question: why do speed limits matter so much in the rain?
questions.a: Wet roads reduce friction, so braking distance increases; at higher speed both thinking and braking distance rise.

questions.q: A 1500 kg car: driving force 4000 N, resistive force 1000 N. Acceleration?
questions.model: Step 1: resultant = 4000 - 1000 = 3000 N. Step 2: a = F ÷ m = 3000 ÷ 1500. Step 3: a = 2 m/s².

questions.q: Weight of a 75 kg astronaut on the Moon (g = 1.6 N/kg)?
Give two factors that increase braking distance.
questions.a: Any two: higher speed, greater mass, wet or icy road, worn tyres, worn brakes.

questions.q: Describe how to investigate the extension of a spring with force, including how to make results accurate. Portal response box.
questions.a: Clamp spring and ruler (1); measure original length (1); add masses 100 g at a time, W = mg (1); measure new length at eye level, calculate extension (1); repeat and average (1); plot force against extension (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first two points: 'Hang the spring from a clamp next to a vertical ruler. Record its original length with a pointer, reading at eye level.'

questions.q: Explain why a skydiver reaches terminal velocity.
questions.a: Weight constant; air resistance increases with speed (1); eventually equals weight (1); resultant force zero so velocity constant (1).

questions.q: Explain what is meant by elastic behaviour.
questions.a: The material returns to its original shape (1) when the force is removed (1).
